title: Beyond Trajectory Similarity: Evaluating Surgical Planning by Protocol Adherence
abstract: arXiv:2601.10455v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Surgical planning is commonly evaluated by trajectory similarity to a single observed execution, a paradigm borrowed from activity anticipation benchmarks such as Ego4D. This conflates two distinct concepts: task completion and protocol adherence and assumes similarity to a completed surgical trajectory implies a valid plan. In surgery, this assumption is flawed: the clinically relevant target is protocol adherence rather than mere completion, and the reference trajectory is only one observed execution that may itself deviate from the protocol. We therefore introduce an evaluation framework grounded in expert-defined protocol rules that directly measures protocol adherence. Under this framework, similarity-based metrics systematically fail: they penalize protocol-adherent plans that deviate from the reference trajectory, while rewarding protocol-violating plans that remain superficially similar to it. translated_title: 超越轨迹相似性：基于手术方案依从性的手术规划评估
translated_abstract: 手术规划通常通过其与单次观察到的执行轨迹的相似性来评估，这一范式借鉴了诸如Ego4D等活动预测基准。这种做法混淆了两个不同的概念——任务完成与方案依从性，并假设与一条已完成的手术轨迹相似即意味着规划有效。在手术领域，这一假设存在缺陷：临床上相关的目标是遵循手术方案而非仅仅完成任务，且参考轨迹只是单次观察到的执行过程，其本身可能就偏离了方案。因此，我们提出了一种基于专家定义的方案规则的评估框架，可直接衡量方案依从性。在该框架下，基于相似性的指标系统性地失效：它们会惩罚那些偏离参考轨迹但符合方案的规划，同时奖励那些表面上与参考轨迹相似却违反方案的规划。对Video-LLMs的进一步评估……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文指出现有基于轨迹相似性的手术规划评估范式混淆了任务完成与方案依从性，并提出首个基于专家定义手术方案规则、直接衡量方案依从性的评估框架，证明相似性指标会系统性误判规划质量。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an evaluation framework grounded in expert-defined protocol rules that directly measures protocol adherence in surgical planning, demonstrating that trajectory-similarity metrics systematically misjudge plan quality.
